scope: All 26 recorded canonical validation cases plus the paired P1 orientation-90 trial. These are project measurements, not publication optimum references or complete-domain coverage. Scratch numerical variants are separate diagnostics and do not replace benchmark values.

p1.description: One real matched-input-vector modern trial; no optimization or model mutation.
p1.high_mass_inference: The model explicitly derives from BESTEST High-Mass Case 930 and contains substantial concrete/brick heat-storage layers. Slow initialization of stored heat is consistent with needing 28 or 34 repeated warmup days under the stringent 0.004 K temperature tolerance. These runs do not isolate thermal mass from weather, orientation, schedules, convection, daylighting or engine changes, so mass is a supported contributor hypothesis, not a proven sole cause.

modern_minus_scratch_85_100_cap.scope: Same physical vector and canonical weather, both strict-success and 100-day caps, but different engine/model versions; scratch historical input is a diagnostic variant.

interpretation.confirmed: A persistent two-day cycle in maximum zone temperature exceeds the single-day warmup criterion. Increasing the cap from25 to100 cannot remove the settled cycle.
interpretation.supported: Convergence under higher HVAC iteration allowance, analytical zone-air integration and a finer effective timestep supports sensitivity to the coupled heat-balance/HVAC numerical solution.
interpretation.not_proven: No individual controller, geometry warning or shading-control defect was isolated as the root cause. Modified-model annual accuracy and benchmark equivalence were not established.
interpretation.other_warnings: Retained model warnings include self-adjacent/interspace surfaces, north/south door multiplier area mismatch, an interior-zone enclosure warning,80percent daylighting-control coverage, zero interior heating sizing and HVAC iteration-limit warnings. They are separate from the single Severe and were not repaired.

Sizing:Parameters averaging window: 6 -> 12 timesteps to preserve 60 minutes
cap_100_days_timestep_12_sizing_12_outpu.diagnostic_objective_status: Strict diagnostics pass, but numerical inputs were changed in a scratch probe; do not treat as the original canonical benchmark objective.
cap_100_days_timestep_12_sizing_12_outpu.final_two_day_comparison_note: These load fractions are reconstructed from matching zone-boundary ESO quantities; a successful run prints flags in EIO but no severe-error residual rows. No exact temperature-extrema residuals are asserted from the different mean-air-temperature output quantity.

supported: The seven original errors all concern peak-load convergence during the annual RunPeriod; every reported temperature comparison passes.
Increasing the maximum warmup days from 25 to 100 retains all seven original failed zones and adds a cooling-load error in PERIMETER_TOP_ZN_1.
Days 81–100 at the original 10-minute zone timestep show a persistent near-period-two load cycle; the final day99/day100 zone-boundary peak ratios reproduce the printed cap100 errors.

The additional top-zone-1 cooling error is amplified by the 8.5 floor asymmetry: a prior zero day remains zero, whereas the current 37.1888 W peak is promoted to 100 W. Other failed peaks exceed 100 W and are not explained by this small-load artifact.

The first 5-minute zone-timestep refinement reaches 100 warmup days with three cooling-load severe errors. Its unchanged 6-timestep sizing averaging window lasts only 30 minutes, so it contains a sizing-duration confound.

The corrected 5-minute zone-timestep refinement also uses 12 sizing averaging steps, preserving the original 60-minute duration. It passes strict diagnostics without severe errors. The warmup-day count and objective are recorded separately; this demonstrates a numerical variant that resolves this sampled failure, without altering the canonical benchmark model.

No canonical benchmark objective is accepted from any probe. The runs with severe errors still exit zero and write annual reports, but the strict wrapper rejects them. The corrected timestep probe passes strict diagnostics and has a diagnostic-only objective because its numerical input differs from the original.
hypotheses_not_isolated: The scheduled fan shutdown with night-cycle operation, thermostatic switches, and autosized VAV system can support the observed cycle, but no individual control change was tested.

The 26.2 dual-floor check prevents this specific 0-to-sub100-W artifact, but cannot by itself explain the modern model passing every other large-load check. Other version and transition changes are not isolated here.

output_and_source_notes.reported_error_precision: Numbers are the exact printed .err values, rounded by EnergyPlus; recomputed history ratios retain more digits.
output_and_source_notes.canonical_Y: Total Source Energy per Conditioned Building Area [MJ/m2], as the 2-decimal annual tabular output; diagnostic-only in all runs here.
output_and_source_notes.history_sampling: Detailed ESO outputs record each HVAC call; peaks at zone-timestep boundaries reproduce the convergence peak values. Arbitrary within-step HVAC maxima can differ and are also retained separately.
output_and_source_notes.eio_load_units: 8.5 .eio labels normalized warmup load differences as W, but source divides by maximum load. The report correctly uses dimensionless names for these averages.
output_and_source_notes.zero_load_passed_metrics: When the current peak is <= 1e-4 W, 8.5 sets Pass without recomputing the comparison field; a printed passed heating comparison can therefore be a stale value. Failed positive-load metrics are reconstructed from history.

official_source.description: Daily extrema, 100 W floor, residual checks, previous-day assignment, capped exit, and normalized EIO loads.
Current and previous heating/cooling peaks are both floored at 100 W before the modern residual check.
Detailed sensible-heating/cooling output variables refer to the convergence source quantities.
